sections.label: THE SILHOUETTE
sections.heading: Inspired by human anatomy.
sections.body: Gradient layers that mirror the body's muscle groups — from toe to heel. A running shoe that reads like a topographic map of motion.

sections.label: MATERIAL
sections.heading: Mesh meets N.P.R. foam.
sections.body: Visible Air cushioning at the heel. A layered mesh upper with neoprene-like panels. Every material chosen for a specific zone of the foot.

sections.label: THE REBELLION
sections.heading: Banned. Fined. Worn anyway.
sections.body: Nike paid the $5,000 fine every game. The shoe that built an empire on a technicality — a colorway that didn't comply with the NBA uniform rule.

sections.label: CONSTRUCTION
sections.heading: Full-grain leather. High ankle.
sections.body: The high-top silhouette was a statement of protection. The perforated toe box, the strap, the Wings logo — each detail deliberate.

sections.label: THE CANVAS
sections.heading: Born on the court. Claimed by the street.
sections.body: Originally a performance basketball shoe, the Dunk became a blank canvas for subcultures — skate, hip-hop, collectors. The simplicity was the point.

sections.label: MATERIAL
sections.heading: Leather over suede. Always.
sections.body: The two-tone construction — a smooth leather base with suede overlays — created a visual language that outlasted every trend it inspired.

sections.label: THE ORIGINAL
sections.heading: 70 years and no apology.
sections.body: Built for frozen pitches in post-war Germany. A rubber gum sole when everyone else used studs. The Samba has never been updated because it never needed to be.

sections.label: CONSTRUCTION
sections.heading: T-toe reinforcement. Gum sole.
sections.body: The T-toe rubber overlay is as structural as it is iconic. The gum sole — unaltered since 1950 — remains the benchmark for indoor court grip.

sections.label: THE SPLIT TONGUE
sections.heading: One problem. One solution.
sections.body: Runners complained of tongue slip. Shigeyuki Mori split it. The resulting design became the most recognizable detail in running shoe history.

sections.label: GEL TECHNOLOGY
sections.heading: Silicone gel in the midsole.
sections.body: The ASICS GEL cushioning system was revolutionary in 1990 — a silicone polymer that absorbed impact across multiple planes of movement.

sections.label: THE FIRST
sections.heading: First basketball shoe with Nike Air.
sections.body: Bruce Kilgore's low-profile design democratized Air technology. It was retired in 1984 and brought back in 1986 by demand — from Baltimore.

sections.label: CONSTRUCTION
sections.heading: Perforated leather. Air unit.
sections.body: The herringbone outsole pattern, the pivot point, the single-piece midsole with encapsulated Air — a construction so right it's been unchanged for 40 years.
